controls.source_problem: For a connected finite oriented graph G and abelian group A, decide whether edge labels d_e are differences d_e=phi(v)-phi(u) of a global vertex potential phi.
controls.target_operational_form: Choose a spanning tree T. For each non-tree edge e, require vanishing of the signed sum of d around its fundamental cycle C_e.

comparison_theorem.statement: A global potential exists iff every fundamental-cycle sum vanishes.
proof: If d is a potential difference, every cycle sum telescopes to zero.
Conversely fix root r and define phi(v) by the signed sum of d along the unique T-path r->v.
Tree edges satisfy d_e=phi(v)-phi(u) by construction.
For a non-tree edge e=(u,v), the fundamental-cycle condition is exactly d_e=phi(v)-phi(u).

proof_leverage_certificate.strict_witness: the global existential consistency condition is equivalent to |E|-|V|+1 explicit fundamental-cycle obstruction checks followed by deterministic tree-path assembly
